transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

Not necessarily. A buzzing pump means it is being powered, but it can buzz without pumping if the impeller is jammed by something just behind the clean filter, or if the drain hose/waste connection is blocked. A new pump is likely only if those are clear and the pump still only hums. 1. Switch off and unplug it; keep towels ready. With the filter removed, shine a torch into the opening and gently try the small impeller vanes with a finger. It should move with a little magnetic resistance, not be solidly stuck. Remove any pin, coin, fabric, etc. you can safely reach. Broken/missing vanes also point to the pump. 2. Check the external drain hose behind the machine for a squash or kink, then where it enters the standpipe or sink waste for a blockage. Don’t run the machine with the hose loose unless it is securely aimed into a suitable container. If the impeller is free and intact and the hose/waste route is clear, but it still buzzes and does not move water, the drain pump becomes the leading suspect. There can still be a blockage in the internal sump hose or a foreign object deeper in the pump, which usually needs access from underneath; that is a sensible point for an appliance engineer rather than buying a pump blind.

did all that. filter out, impeller spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected. torch shows one fin looks snapped. hose and sink waste are both clear. coil reads about 170 ohms. so its the pump yeah? just want to confirm before i order

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
Yes — on that evidence, the drain pump is the very likely fault. The impeller should have distinct magnetic stepping resistance as it turns; one that spins freely as though disconnected, with a snapped vane, points to the impeller/rotor having failed. The buzz and no drainage fit that as well. The roughly 170-ohm coil reading does not clear the pump: it only shows the winding is not open-circuit. A mechanically failed impeller can still give a plausible resistance reading and hum. With the filter, external hose and sink waste clear, replacing the complete drain-pump assembly is reasonable. A hidden obstruction in the sump hose is still a small possibility, but it would not explain the free-spinning, damaged impeller nearly as well. I cannot confirm an exact compatible pump from that model reference alone, so match the replacement through Hoover's official spares service using the full product/I-D label from the machine, or have an appliance engineer supply and fit it. If fitting involves accessing underneath or removing panels, isolate and unplug the washer-dryer first; an engineer is the safer route if you are not comfortable dealing with residual water and internal connections.

candidates: Obstruction in or immediately behind the drain-pump impeller (high)
Blocked or kinked drain hose / household waste connection (medium)
